question: Is the three-component pipeline (context-enriched supervision + adaptive repair + lower-hop RL) too confounded to support a clean claim, such that the investigation should scope down to a single testable component?
description: Each component is a separate intervention with its own failure modes; running all three jointly makes it impossible to attribute gains and multiplies the chance of a null result. The likely refinement is to first establish the context-enrichment effect alone under matched controls, then add repair, then RL.
confidence_basis: Grounded in explicit evidence that the auxiliary components are separately precedented and in two recorded assumptions that the pipeline depends on; the judgement that the bundle cannot support a clean claim is an inference about experimental design rather than a measured result.
rationale: Scoping decisions at this point determine whether the contribution is a clean, attributable result or an uninterpretable bundle.
resolution: Resolved in favour of scoping down. The evidence shows the pipeline cannot support a single clean claim: the repair loop depends on the unevidenced locality assumption that one-hop failures localize bad base facts (C010), the three stages are assumed independently ablatable without evidence (C011), and both auxiliary components are separately precedented in prior work — intermediate supervision (NSM) and RL for multi-hop KG reasoning (KG-Hopper) — so the bundled contribution adds attribution risk without adding novelty (C012). Meanwhile the context-relevance question is separately testable and has a clean negative-result path (C014, C015, C019). Enacted by direction D001 and the revised M001: a gated, staged protocol with a single primary hypothesis (Stage 1: does context relevance beat an equal-length irrelevant control under matched budgets?), a conditional repair hypothesis (Stage 2, only if one-hop failures are shown to localize base-fact errors), and a deferred RL hypothesis (Stage 3, only if supervised lower-hop training leaves a transfer gap).
